3.2.9         Error handling for Auto-Configuration
Error handling mechanism for auto configuration is used to cover the cases in which the agent could not be
configured successfully, for example, when the Controller sync the new configuration to all agents, some agents
disconnect from current network, then when these agents reconnect to the MAP network, the configuration will
not sync on these agents.
The error handling mechanism is mainly depend on the detection of topology change, when detecting of an
agent leaving, the topology service in 1905daemon will delete the leaf that represents the removed agent from
the topology tree, and also delete all its child leaves, when these agents reconnect to current network, controller
will regard these agents as new agents that are not configured, then if these agents do not start auto
configuration procedure by themselves within 30 seconds, the Controller will start auto configuration renew
procedure.

                  c.   Agent3 reconnect to controller, the controller will regard agent3, 4, 5, 6 as the new
                       agents, if these agents do not start auto configuration procedure within 30 seconds, the
                       controller will start to send renew message to each of them to trigger auto configuration.

3.3           Mediatek Multi-AP Controller Connectivity with Non-MAP devices
Mediatek Multi-AP solution provides provision for the controller to be connected with Non-MAP device through
both Ethernet as well as WiFi interfaces. This helps Mediatek Multi-AP network to get WAN connectivity through
Non-MAP devices as well.

This feature is also commonly called Third Party connection.

3.3.1         Ethernet BH link for controller with non-MAP uplink device
To get controller connection with non-MAP AP, expectations here is that Ethernet should be plugged on WAN
interface from controller to that non-MAP AP.

3.3.2         Wireless BH for controller with non-MAP uplink device:
A Controller’s ApCli interface connection is established with the non-MAP AP. This uses the same best AP
selection algorithm as used by ApCli interfaces of any other agent. However, a MAP device will never be selected
as the target AP for a controller’s ApCli interface. If the feature is enabled, and BH configuration profiles are saved
for a controller, the Mediatek Multi-AP solution will continue to scan unless a connection is formed with a target
AP. The scan process can be stopped by disabling the feature dynamically. If the feature is enabled and profiles
were not previously available, controller ApCli interfaces will remain in idle state and scan will not be performed.
There are two ways through which the profile can be made available to the controller.

1.    Trigger WPS:
               • The ApCli interfaces of controller can connect and get profile by forming a WPS push button
                   connection. The profile thus received will be stored on Non-Volatile memory and will be
                   available after reboot.

2.    Store profile directly on non-volatile memory:
               • The profile can be stored directly on Non-volatile memory as detailed in below sections.

The feature needs to be enabled on the controller using additional configurations in configuration file and APIs
are required to trigger connection of a MAP controller with a Non-MAP Wireless AP. By default this feature is
disabled.

•   Auto role detection. Check on every device that if it can ping 8.8.8.8/208.67.222.222 with fixed length 88
    and block ping with 8.8.8.8/208.67.222.222 from downstream device.
•   If ping can success, move to send search state. Send auto-configuration search message on Ethernet and wifi
    backhaul sta interface every 5s to check if controller is already exist and schedule a 30s timer to decide role.
    Meanwhile collecting auto configuration search message from the other device. If ping can’t success, keep
    on ping.
•   If it receives auto-configuration response message, change own role to agent and cancel timer scheduled in
    auto role stage and unblock ping with 8.8.8.8/208.67.222.222 from downstream device. If it doesn’t receive
    any auto-configuration response message during auto role detect stage, after timeout, check if its own almac
    is the biggest among the data base of receiving auto configuration search message, change its role to
    controller otherwise change role to agent.

3.6           Multi-AP Renew
Multi-AP renew is a mechanism to update configuration information of operating bss both at controller and agent.
It supports both backhaul and fronthaul bss renew.

3.6.1         Main flow of first time set-up
1.    Once mapd has started up, it calls lib1905 API _1905_Set_Read_Bss_Conf_and_Renew to trigger local bss
      setting.
2.    1905 daemon read wts_bss_info_config and send wireless setting event to wapp to set new
      ssid/authmode/encryption/password/bss role into driver.
3.    In wapp,
      a. If the setting is the same with the old one, it just skips it.
      b. If the setting is updated compared to the old one, it applies to the new one.

     c. If the previously configured interface is not configured this time, it disables that interface.
4.   Driver just executes the cmd sent by wapp.

3.6.2         Main flow of wireless setting update
1.   UI changes bss configuration information and updates wts_bss_info_config file.
2.   UI call libmapd API mapd_renew to start renew procedure.
3.   mapd calls lib1905 API _1905_Set_Read_Bss_Conf_and_Renew_v2 to start renew state machine.
4.   renew state machine in 1905 dump the topology tree into a stack structure with preorder traversal algorithm.
5.   renew state machine pops out agent one by one stored in the stack and sends unicast renew message it.
6.   Agents do auto-configuration one by one to get and update new wireless setting.
7.   After      all  agents   renew      done,   1905     sends     message       to   Mapd      with      MsgId
     _1905_SET_WIRELESS_SETTING_EVENT.
8.   After all agents renew done, Mapd sends command with Cmd ID WAPP_USER_SET_WIRELESS_SETTING to
     wapp to trigger updating local bss setting.

Note:
The main difference of renew between R1/R2 and R3 is that
1. Controller send AP Autoconfig renew to each agent, then M1 and M2 between Controller and agents for R1/R2
renew
2. Controller send BSS reconfiguration trigger message to each agent, then BSS Configuration Request, BSS
configuration response, BSS Configuration Result message between controller and Agents for R3 renew

3.6.4         Limitations
As the controller has to renew all the agents one by one, and it will take a few seconds (8~10 seconds per agent)
to renew the whole Multi-AP network. How long it will take depends on the amount of agent in the Multi-AP
network. User should not trigger a new renew process before the previous one is done, or else the controller
fails to renew all the agents.

3.6.5         Customer Feature to Enable/Disable SSID on Specific Interface
Customer has the requirement to runtime enable or disable SSID on specific interface of the whole mesh network.
This is due to customer bind the wireless mode or other Wi-Fi parameter to interface. In this way SSID is bond to
interface and they need operate the specific interface.

Take 5G setting for instance, with the first setup, the mesh network is configured as bellow on both Controller
and Agents:
                    Rax0---11ax--- Multi-AP-5LG-1
                    Rax1--11ac--- Multi-AP-5LG-2
                    Rax2---11an--- Multi-AP-5LG-3
                    Rax3---11ax--- Multi-AP-5LG-4
If user wants to disable rax1 on both Controller and Agents, the user could do following step to update the setting:
          ⚫ Set command on Controller and wait a few seconds to make it done.
                    mapd_cli /tmp/mapd_ctrl set_bss_prio
                    "ra0;ra1;ra2;ra3;apcli0;rax0;rax2;rax3;rax1;apclix0;rai0;rai1;rai2;rai3;apclii0"
          or directly
                    mapd_cli /tmp/mapd_ctrl set_bss_prio "rax0;rax2;rax3;rax1;apclix0"
this command will trigger Controller to update local BSS priority and, in the meanwhile, to synchronize the BSS
priority setting to Agents by Mediate vendor message.
          ⚫ Delete the wireless setting by Multi-AP-5LG-2 and do renew
          ⚫ Once renew is done, the new setting would be:
                Rax0---11ax--- Multi-AP-5LG-1
                Rax1--11ac--- BSS stop
                Rax2---11an--- Multi-AP-5LG-3
                Rax3---11ax--- Multi-AP-5LG-4
If user wants to enable rax1, he could add one wireless setting and do renew. Once the renew procedure is done,
the new setting would be:
                    Rax0---11ax--- Multi-AP-5LG-1
                    Rax1--11ac--- BSS start with new SSID
                    Rax2---11an--- Multi-AP-5LG-3
                    Rax3---11ax--- Multi-AP-5LG-4

3.8             Automatic BH Switching between Ethernet and Wi-Fi
MAP Turnkey provides two variants for BH link switch between Ethernet and Wi-Fi. MAP-Turnkey supports
automatic switching between Wi-Fi and Ethernet.
After 2020, the officially released EasyMesh can support automatic Ethernet/Wi-Fi backhaul switching and
Ethernet onboarding between two agents.
The flow is as follows:
Switching from Wi-Fi to Ethernet:
        1. Agent connects to controller using Wi-Fi BH.
        2. Ethernet is plugged between agent and controller.
        3. Agent disconnects Wi-Fi BH link and uses Ethernet connection for communication.

Switching from Ethernet to Wi-Fi
        1. Initially Agent and Controller are connected via Ethernet link.
        2. Ethernet is unplugged between Controller and Agent.
        3. Agent detects Ethernet unplug and re-triggers connection on Wi-Fi BH link.

While switching from Ethernet to WiFi, Agent will always attempt to keep the topology unchanged. Hence it will
attempt to connect to the controller for three times. If the connection with controller is not restored in three

3.12.1        Introduction
Spatial reuse operation addressed in Wi-Fi 6 is to allow the medium to be reused more often between OBSSs in
dense deployment scenarios by the early identification of signals from overlapping basic service sets (OBSSs) and
interference management.

Currently SR operation is verified only on AX4200 Panther platform.

transmission, which result in Spatial Reuse is not applicable under Mesh Scenario.

prohibited to Spatial Reuse internal traffic. If criteria have met, it can operate as 2 nd phase, which is MTK Mesh

4       MAP Network Maintenance

4.1           Introduction

All the Turnkey features for network maintenance and stability form a part of this chapter.
Mainly they are:
1. Network Healing: which aims to restore network connectivity
2. Network optimization: which is a mechanism to automatically form the best topology based on the current
     conditions.
3. BH link steering and prioritizations: which gives flexibility to the user to give more priority to a particular
     BH.
4. Loop detection and avoidance: which is introduced to solve circle topology

4.2              Network Healing
Network healing feature aims to restore network connectivity if one of the Agents goes down or backhaul link is
broken.
If backhaul link of an Agent is broken either due to its upstream Multi-AP device going down or due to any other
reason, then the Agent will try to search for other Multi-AP devices in the network to which it can connect.
Mediatek solution for network healing provides an efficient mechanism to restore network connectivity with
minimum disruptions.
The link failover feature developed by Mediatek considers the following parameters for making new connection:
     • Best Uplink AP selection based on RSSI, number of hops, uplink rate etc.
     • Avoid Repeater to Repeater looping.

To achieve this, Mediatek Multi-AP devices add a vendor specific IE in the beacon and probe response to show:
    • Distance from root
    • Connectivity to controller
Based on these parameters, the agent tries to connect to the best available Agent in the network.

Steps followed by the Multi-AP device for network healing:
    • Multi-AP device gets a trigger of backhaul link disconnected
    • It will trigger a scan to find out the backhaul bss available in the network
    • Based on the scan results and received RSSI of the probe response/beacons of the backhaul bss, Multi-
          AP device will find the best candidate backhaul BSS to connect to using a proprietary method.
    • After it has found the best backhaul bss, it will attempt connection.
    • If connection fail, it will move to the next best bss
    • If connection success, then it will update the vendor specific IE and data will be resumed.

Note: In case of 3rd Party device, Mediatek Multi-AP devices will not consider uplink rate as there will be no
Mediatek MAP vendor specific IE in the beacon and probe response. So in that case the best uplink ap selection
will not consider uplink rate.

For MAP R3 device, in network healing if DPP connection has to be formed then first DPP Network Introduction
Protocol is done and then bSTA connection is formed.

4.3.2         Backhaul Link Prioritization
The Backhaul link selection at the agents happens via MediaTek’s Multi-AP Best AP selection algorithm.
When WPS connection is triggered on enrollee device, it will scan on all the bands and find out all the channels
on which WPS registrar is present (with same UUID). Based on this scan result, device will select an interface on
which WPS handshake will happen.

WPS registrar provides profiles of all the available Backhaul BSS on each of the bands during the WPS handshake.
Based on these profiles, the enrollee agent selects the best suited profile based on the available bands.

But it is also possible for user to give more preference to a particular Backhaul link using the below prioritization
techniques. Ethernet is always given the highest priority and this cannot be altered. So if Ethernet connection
exists between two devices then BH will always be ethernet and not wifi.

But priority can be set for other bands. Like for example if there are 3 bands 2G , 5GL and 5GH, then by default
priority setting in config file is kept as 3 for 2G , 1 for 5GL and 1 for 5GH. This means that 5GH and 5GL are given
highest and equal priority i.e. 1 and 2G is given lowest priority i.e. 3. The interface on which backhaul connection
will be made depends on this priority. If an interface is programmed with priority 0, we will not attempt
connection on that interface ever.

Note that just by setting the priority for a radio band as the highest, does not guarantee that the BH link will be
formed at that band. Since the best AP selection also considers other factors also. Please see the main feature
flow in below section.
It should also be noted that for proper DFS functionality we expect that at least one BH on non-DFS band is
always present. Hence it is discouraged to program priority of 2.4G band as 0.

Mediatek solution provides Automatic Backhaul link selection mechanism. A backhaul link priority is configured:
Ethernet > 5G > 2.4G as per default. This can be changed dynamically as well. It should be noted that changing
backhaul priority will impact the existing connection and hence should be triggered only on stable networks.
Backhaul switching should be avoided immediately after connection and should be triggered after auto
configuration is complete. Also triggering backhaul preference in quick succession will impact connection process
of previously triggered command to change priority hence it should be avoided.

▪   BH Link prioritization is a mediatek proprietary feature. So only a mediatek agent can support it. Most of
    the logic is present agent side.
▪   Network Optimization should be disabled via cli command before using Backhaul steer or band switching.

4.3.2.1       Main Flow
Flow at the Enrollee Agent
    1. When WPS is triggered on the device, it will start scan and find out all the bands on which WPS
         registrar are active and have the same UUID
    2. If it finds registrars with more than 1 UUID, then it stops WPS on all interfaces due to PBC overlap.
    3. If it finds multiple WPS PBC registrars with same UUID, then it triggers WPS handshake on one band.
    4. It gets multiple Backhaul BSS profiles in M8 of WPS handshake. The backhaul profiles contains the
         following parameters :
              a. SSID
              b. AuthMode
              c. EncryptType
              d. PSK
    5. Above configurations are saved in nvram/config file for future use. These parameters are not band
         specific. Agents need to scan for these configs on all the bands/channels
    6. After the device gets multiple Backhaul BSS profiles and finds them in scan results, it applies the best
         Backhaul BSS selection procedure and finds the best BSS to connect to.
    7. According to the algorithm, 5G band is given preference over 2.4G band for backhaul link creation.
    8. 1 being the highest priority and 3 being the lowest.
    9. Additionally we have provision for configuring minimum RSSI values which will be considered at the
         time of best AP selection.
    10. If the minimum RSSI Threshold value for a band is configured, the best AP calculation can be
         performed thrice, as explained below:
              a. First calculations will consider only the higher priority band and APs with considerably good
                   RSSI.
              b. If a best AP is not found in above step, we will consider APs on second priority band and with
                   considerably good RSSI.
              c. If an AP is found in second step, by tuning the RSSI correctly, we can safely assume that AP on
                   second priority band will provide better “t-put” than first priority band.
              d. If the AP is not found in second step as well, we will consider all the APs on all priority bands
                   and pick the AP with maximum “t-put” as candidate AP without considering the RSSI
                   threshold programmed.
    11. It should be noted that if connection is not completed in 30 seconds after triggering connection, or if
         the connection is rejected by the peer AP, the peer AP will blacklisted for further connections for
         5mins. This means that the AP will not be considered in subsequent connection attempts for next 5
         mins.
    12. For 6E case, Agent will scan only on PSC channels. If Controller is setup on non-PSC channel then there

4.4           Network Optimization
Network optimization is a mechanism to automatically form the best topology based on the current conditions.
This mechanism is completely controlled and implemented at the controller. Hence, it can also be referred to as
centralized network optimization.
         • Controller will contain the entire information about the network.
         • Controller will gain this network information by making its agents do an off-channel scan.
         • Using all the scan results the controller will decide the final optimized network topology.
         • The controller will realize this new topology by sending out backhaul steer command to all the
             agents whose BH is changed.

For network optimization in MAP R2, Scan Request (to collect scan results from the agents in the network) will
be sent only if that MAP R2 agent supports fresh scan in their scan capabilities as per MAP R2 specification.
Otherwise for MAP R1 device Network optimization scan will be done using proprietary off channel scan
mechanism. Network optimization relies on present devices and environment only and cannot use old scan
results.

4.4.1         Network Optimization for MLDs in mesh network
For Mesh devices which are 802.11be MLO capable, the network optimization internal algorithm will consider
the information for all the MLO links which one mesh device can make with the other using cumulative MLD
scoring.
     • Using this MLD score final optimized network topology will be decided. Hence there will be more
         chances of an MLD agent to make connection with another MLD agent/controller as compared to a non-
         MLD device when in a mixed network.
     • Finally, the BH steer command will be sent to all the Agents whose backhaul needs to be changed or
         primary backhaul needs to be changed.
     • In this command the target BSSID will be the best out of all the MLD links possible with the uplink device .
         This BSSID will be chosen so that the primary link in the MLO connection is formed on this BSS.
     • However in current design 5G BSS is never given to form the primary link, even if its score is coming as
         the best, for avoiding traffic interruption because of DFS channels CAC time.

4.4.2         Trigger conditions
Network optimization is triggered in the following scenarios:
       • Uplink Rate variation
                o Controller will trigger network optimization if the uplink rate of each device varies a lot
                     from the previous uplink rate, in the current topology.
       • Topology change:
                o Controller triggers network opt. with any change in topology
                           ▪ Any new device joins the network
                           ▪ Any device leaves the network
       • Post DFS channel selection:

4.4.3         Fail Safe Mechanism for network optimization
There is a failsafe mechanism that will trigger network optimization in every 2 minutes interval in case BH stays
on 2G only. As soon as BH is switched to 2G, it will set a timer function, that will check if the BH is still present
on 2G, it will trigger network optimization. This mechanism is disabled by default. To enable this mechanism,
below mapd config parameter ‘NetworkOptPrefer5Gover2G' need to be set to ‘1’. The number of times this
periodic mechanism need to be executed can also be configured using another parameter
‘NetworkOptPrefer5Gover2GRetryCnt’.

         NetworkOptPrefer5Gover2G=<0/1>
         NetworkOptPrefer5Gover2GRetryCnt=<1/2/3/….so on>

4.4.4         Important points
1.   Network Optimization gets automatically disabled when a manual BH steer command is given at the
     controller to change the network. So in this case if user wants to run network opt again then you can enable

     Enabled on any device in the network.

3.   Network optimization does not run for devices with ETH backhaul. However, other devices with Wi-Fi BH
     can choose to connect with ETH backhaul device on the basis of best score.

4.5.1         Main Flow
•   When ETH plug in, the agent will check if it can access controller based on topology database. If it is, the
    agent will trigger auto-configuration by itself.
•   When ETH plug out, the agent will trigger scan and find the best AP to connect.
•   When ETH plug in, the device will do loop detection to find if there is a ring in topology (two or more paths
    to controller). The loop detection rules are
         o Count up the current hopcnt (WIFI hopcnt) to controller from the WIFI backhaul and the hopcnt
             (ETH hopcnt) to controller from the ETH backhaul. Take WIFI backhaul connection as 1 hop and
             take ETH connection as 0 hop.
         o If ETH hopcnt > WIFI hopcnt, do nothing. Let the peer device do the decision.
         o If ETH hopcnt < wifi hopcnt, break WIFI backhaul connection.
         o If ETH hopcnt == WIFI hopcnt, the device with smaller almac breaks WIFI backhaul connection. The
             compared device locates in its eth neighbor side and it has different WIFI backhaul neighbor and
             ETH neighbor.

5       Database and Diagnostics

5.1           Introduction

Database maintenance and diagnostics are an integral part of MediaTek’s Turnkey solution. This chapter explains
about all of them.
Databases supported are:
    1. Topology Database: Information about all the MAP supported nodes in the network.
    2. Client Database: Information about all the clients present in the network.
    3. Wi-Fi 6 Support: Information of the Wi-Fi 6 capable Agents and Wi Fi 6 capable associated STAs.
    4. DPP configurations: Information used to form DPP connection.

Diagnostics supported are:
    5. Data elements: Set of diagnostic parameters about radio/BSS/clients etc. which are mandatory as per
        MAP R2 specification. Some new parameters were also added in MAP R3 version.

5.2           Topology Database
5.2.1         Feature Details
      1905 Topology messages are used to learn about network topology by all nodes in the network. Following
      are topology messages:
      1.    Topology Discovery: Neighbor-Multicast (ieee-1905 std)
            a. Sent by each node on all interfaces periodically
            b. Consumed by direct neighbor, never forwarded
            c. Helps build DIRECT NEIGHBORS
      2.    Topology Notification: Multicast-Relay (MAP extension 17.1.5 1905 Topology Notification message)
            a. Sent whenever a node detects change on its topology or interface i.e. new link up/down, STA
                associated/disconnected etc.
            b. Relayed by all nodes, nodes discard previously seen Notifications to prevent loop
      3.    Topology Query: Unicast (ieee-1905 std)
            a. Sent by a node to a specific destination to query of its current state and interfaces
            b. Periodically sent for each entry in Database, age out the unresponsive nodes
      4.    Topology Response: Unicast (MAP extension 17.1.4 1905 Topology Response message)
            a.   Sent in response to Topology Query to querying node
            b.   Provides its current state
            c.   Used by both Direct and Distant Neighbors
            d.   Has following TLVs
                 (a) Device Info
                 (b) Capabilities
                 (c) List of Legacy Neighbors (for each of its interfaces)
                 (d) 1905 Device Neighbors on its interfaces
                 (e) Attached WLAN Stations

5.3           Client Database
5.3.1         Feature details
An AP must be able to handle various clients. Legacy clients do not support 802.11v BTM transition and therefore
11v BTM request is not applicable. Some newer clients support 802.11v BTM but their behaviors vary depending
on the implementation.
Per the experiments, some 11v-capable clients always followed BTM requests from the AP and others only
accepted the requests conditionally. Therefore, the AP must find a suitable steering method for each client
adaptively.
An algorithm runs to learn client capabilities from each steering result and becomes better as more steering
occurs. Algorithm adapts the 11k, 11v characteristics based on previous results and takes better steer decisions
next time

The learnings from this algorithm are stored in a client database and are synchronized among the Multi-AP
devices to take better steering decisions.

A total of 128 client entries are maintained by each Multi-AP device. If the client database is full and a new entry
needs to be added, a client entry which was least recently used in the client database is removed.

    ▪     Multi-AP R3 improving its comprehensive diagnostic information, increasing the scope of metrics

          these metrics.
    ▪     R3 DE feature includes the following :
              • Controller use AP Capability Query to get Diagnostics Information.

5.4.2.1       R3 DE Spec Details
    ▪     AP Capability Report Message:
              • If a Multi-AP Agent that implements Profile-3 sends an AP Capability Report message, it shall
                 also perform the following:
                       ▪ Include one Device Inventory TLV in the AP Capability Report message.
              • If a Multi-AP device that implements Profile-3 sends an AP Capability Report message, then
                 for the following fields in the Device Inventory TLV:
                       ▪ the Serial Number string shall remain fixed over the lifetime of the device, including
                           across firmware updates
                       ▪ if a Multi-AP Agent supports multiple firmware images, the Software Version string
                           shall be the software version of the active firmware image
                       ▪ to allow version comparisons, the Software Version string should be in the form of
                           dot-delimited integers, where each successive integer represents a more minor
                           category of variation. For example, 3.0.21 where the components mean:
                           Major.Minor.Build
                       ▪ if a Multi-AP Agent supports multiple execution environments, the ExecutionEnv
                           string shall be the active execution environment

6          Steering

6.1            Introduction
Mediatek’s Multi-AP Turnkey solution provides a centralized approach in which the controller is responsible for
the client steering decisions for all the clients connected to any device of the entire multi-ap network.

Centralized steering includes:
    1. Multi -AP Steering: Steering client from one MAP device to another
    2. Band Steering: Steering client from one radio band to another on same MAP device
    3. Client DB: Connected client database management at Controller



6.2            Centralized Steering feature details
Centralized Steering requires the following mechanisms:

      1.   Maintenance of topology database:

      Topology database is maintain other AP’s BSSID, channel info, PHY capability etc. It will be used by algorithm
      to select the threshold (on the Root, the threshold is lower to delay AP steering), initiate coordination among
      APs, to estimate MCS rate and airtime for best AP selection etc.

      2.   Coordination between MAP devices:

      Mechanism between Aps to do the RSSI measurement and setup blacklist for best possibility steering

      3.   Centralized client server model:

      Controller is the server and the agents the client. Controller being responsible for steering decisions requires
      the multi-ap agents to send the metrics information periodically. It also requires the agent to follow client
      steering request triggered by the controller after a steering decision has been made at the controller. The
      controller chooses a new MAP agent periodically for load balancing and upgrade steering. However, the
      controller performs multi-ap steering or band steering (performance of STA downgraded) when the STA
      Metrics Reporting RCPI threshold trigger is received from the agent to which the client is connected. Load
      balancing includes channel overload and moving STA to a better band (2.4G --> 5G). To achieve this using
      MAP specification, following messages are used:
               a. Steering Policy and AP Metric Reporting: Controller send Policy Config Request message
                     (17.1.8 Multi-AP Policy Config Request message) to configure the new detected agent (when
                     new agent join).
                           i. Steering policy: Set Agent Initiated RSSI-based Steering to disallowed to disable
                              steering decisions being taken at the agent.
                          ii. Channel Utilization Threshold: align single AP band steering parameters.
                         iii. RSSI Steering Threshold: depends on role (LowRSSIAPSteerEdge_Root/
                              LowRSSIAPSteerEdge_RE), it will be different threshold settings.
                         iv. AP Metrics Reporting Interval: The interval at which the agent will send ap metrics
                              report periodically. Configured via MetricRepIntv in the /etc/mapd_strng.conf file(set
                              to 10 seconds default).
                          v. STA Metrics Reporting RCPI threshold: A non zero value will enable the agent rcpi
                              monitor mechanism. When the client RCPI crosses the threshold the agent will send
                              an unsolicited sta link metrics response to the controller.
                         vi. STA Metrics Reporting RCPI Hysteresis Margin Override: The purpose of the hysteresis
                              margin is to prevent an agent from sending the unsolicited sta link metrics response

6.2.1         Decision for Multi-AP Steering or Standalone Band Steering
    1.   On 5GHz, if RSSI (or rate for active client) is lower than standalone downgrade threshold, attempt
         standalone downgrade steering
    2.   For idle client, RSSI < RSSISteeringEdge_DG
    3.   For active client, RSSI < RSSICrossingThreshold_DG || MCS < MCSCrossingThreshold_DG
    4.   On 2.4GHz, if RSSI (and rate for active client) are higher than standalone upgrade threshold, attempt
         standalone upgrade steering
    5.   For idle client, RSSI > RSSISteeringEdge_UG
    6.   For active client, RSSI > RSSICrossingThreshold_UG && MCS > MCSCrossingThreshold_UG
    7.   Others, go through Multi-AP steering procedures

6.2.2         Band Steering
Band steering as the name implies means that client is steered from one band to the other on the same MAP
device. Hence it is also known as Standalone Steering.
There are two primary types of steering that are supported: -
         • Idle post-association steering
         • Active post-association steering.
                   o Active Non-Overloaded Steering
                   o Active Overloaded Steering



6.2.2.1       Band steering for MLD clients
Band steering is not supported for a multi link device (MLD) client. For the MLD client Band steering is not
applicable, as multi link device is expected to be already connected with multi links, so switching the primary
link on the same device via band steering will not give much advantage.

6.2.2.2       Idle post-association steering
          •   An idle client is defined as a client for which the sum of Avg Tx Bytes/sec and Avg Rx Bytes/sec is
              less that Activitythreshold
          •   An idle client can be steered by either of the two methods:-
                   o Forced Steering: Disconnect + Deauth
                   o BTM Steering: IEEE80211v BSS Transition Management
          •   IDLE Clients with recent enough RSSI on 5G band, whose estimated non-serving RSSI(2.4Ghz) has
              fallen below RSSISteeringEdge_DG are forced steered/ BTM steered to 2.4G band if the 2.4G
              channel is non-overloaded. If the RSSI is quite old, the RSSI is refreshed by triggering a series of
              NULL frames to the IDLE client. If IDLE client is known to fail BTM steering, forced steering is
              attempted.
          •   IDLE Clients with recent enough RSSI on 2.4Ghz band, whose non-serving RSSI(RSSI on 5G) has
              increased above RSSISteeringEdge_UG are forced steered/ BTM steered to 5G band if the 5G
              channel is non-overloaded. If the RSSI is quite old, the RSSI is refreshed by triggering a series of
              NULL frames to the IDLE client. If IDLE client is known to fail BTM steering, forced steering is
              attempted.

Multi-AP steering is a mechanism to attempt to move a client from 1 AP to another in a Multi-AP Network
environment. Best BSS selection for steering client to another MAP dev firstly requires channel measurement.
Based on Channel measurement (Radio Resource measurement /Beacon measurement) score is calculated for

6.2.3.1       Selection of Measurement Channels
In multi-AP steering we need to perform the measurement to find out the AP which can provide best
performance to client. Firstly, we need to decide the channel that wants to measure. It will consist two cases.
     - Case 1: if client cannot support RRM, then the measurement channel will be same as current serving
         channel (to perform Airmonitor)
     - Case 2: if the client can support RRM, it will follow the filters to determine the channel.
         ◼ Filter 1: same channel as serving channel
         ◼ Filter 2: 6G channel first
         ◼ Filter 3: 5G channel second
         ◼ Filter 4: lowest channel utilization
For active clients, all overloaded channels will be excluded.

6.2.3.2       Selection of Best BSS
Based on measurement results, select the BSS based on the following rules:

1.   RSSI difference between the current BSS and the target BSS and Link Capacity is better than the current link.
           i. The difference should be greater than a threshold
          ii. The threshold is different for upstream devices and downstream devices
2.   Link Capacity between the current BSS Link capacity threshold and target BSS.
           i. Link capacity of the target BSS should be greater than the current BSS link capacity threshold.
          ii. Link capacity threshold is link capacity on current RSSI + RSSI margin.
3.   Upstream BSS is preferred over downstream and peer BSS (same distance from root)
4.   6G band BSS is preferred over 5G BSS. 5G band BSS is preferred over 2.4G band BSS.
5.   BSS on channel with lowest channel utilization is preferred.


6.2.3.3       Selection of Best BSS for MLD Clients
1.   All the above point in section 6.2.3.2 are also valid in case if clients are MLO capable.
2.   For a MLD client the steering decision is taken after considering the cumulative score of all the MLD links it
     is cable of making, hence for this reason 11k measurement/air monitoring and score calculation etc need to
     consider the channels for all multi links.
     For the MLD client Band steering is not applicable, as multi link device is expected to be already connected
     with multi links, so switching the primary link on the same device via band steering will not give much
     advantage.

6.2.3.4       Steer coordination in Multi-AP environment
     There will be two reasons (at least) we need the coordination among APs.
     1. For the best probability of steering success, it is necessary that the controller initiates the steering
         coordinate with the other nodes in the network so that they can install blacklists and withhold probe
         responses as appropriate (MAP 17.2.31 Client Association Control Request message)

     2.   Without this coordination, the legacy steering mechanism would often lead to the client associating on
          a different BSS than intended in cases where signal strength is similar between Root and RE or the
          client’s own BSS selection algorithm prefers a different BSS than the target one. Even steering using
          802.11v BSS Transition Management Request (at least with current clients) is not as reliable without the
          steering coordination.

     3.   To position the client with improved WiFi Network performance by steering the clients to a better-
          serving AP through a better RSSI. If the client does not support 802.11k beacon measurement (or a
          client that fails for consecutive attempts of 802.11k beacon report), we need AP coordination to monitor
          the client RSSI and report to initiating AP (MAP 17.1.20 Unassociated STA Link Metrics Query message)

6.2.3.5       Tri-band detection
Since the controller is responsible for taking steering decisions, the controller will maintain a centralized client
database.
We currently rely on probe request and association to determine if the client is tri band capable.
In the centralized steering design, the client database will be updated based on
          - Probe Requests received by Controller
However not all clients can be identified as dual band based on the above method as some clients may not be in
vicinity of the Controller for it to receive their probe requests.

For all such cases, we try to detect whether the client is dual band capable or not by utilizing the supported
operating classes element during the client association phase which is mandatory if the client is MBO capable. If
operating class IE is not found in association request, then we send rrm request. We exclude the currently
operated band for rrm. If client send proper rrm response on another band, controller will update database for
the client.
If there is no supported operating classes element, we initially assume that all the clients are tri-band capable
and allow the tri-band steering for all clients. Based on the steering attempts failures beyond a configured
threshold (default is 5), we mark it as single band or dual band.

The threshold can be configured via the CentSteerMaxBSFail parameter in /etc/mapd_strng.conf.

6.2.5         Limitations
    1.   Since the centralized steering design relies on the controller to take the steering decisions for the
         entire network, the STA steering time will be impacted by the processing delay taken at the controller
         (slower then distributed steering).
    2.   Pre-assoc Band Steering is not supported with centralized steering in MAP. It cannot be supported
         because there is no mechanism provided by the MAP specification for the agents to share probe
         requests with the controller before association attempt is made to take any pre-assoc decisions.
    3.   Band Steering during CAC cannot be handled.
    4.   802.11r based fast transition not supported across bands. If FT is enabled on the DBDC AP, FT capable
         station, when band steered, would fall back on non-FT Association.

7       Multi-AP Channel planning

7.1           Introduction

Mediatek Multi-AP Channel Planning is a centralized feature which runs at the controller. The aim of this feature
is that controller converges the entire MAP network devices and all their radios on a common channel.

Channel planning is a feature which was available in map R1 version also, but it has been enhanced in MAP R2
release by making use of information that we can gather in MAP R2 version.

In MAP R1, aim was to converge the entire map network on a common channel, at each radio. But in MAP R2,
first we try to find the best channel amongst all the preferred channels based on channel conditions, and then
converge all devices to use this best channel for each radio. In MAP R3 and R4 , all existing features of R1 and R2
are available.

                                                                    vary for current channel and MAP network is in

This convergent channel planning approach helps in ensuring that a MAP device is able to monitor the
transmissions by a station which is connected to a different MAP device present in the network. It is focused on
enhancing the efficiency of client steering. AP Steering of legacy clients (devices which don’t support 802.11k)
can happen only if all devices are on same channel. AP Steering utilizes air monitor feature for monitoring
Unassociated Client RSSI on same channel for handoff procedures. Placing Fronthaul BSSs on same channel will
also provide faster handoff of roaming clients.

Mt7603 can’t support channel planning R2 feature, as it can’t get the accurate parameters needed for choosing
the best channel. Mt7603 will report zero for edcca, my tx air time, my rx air time, obss time and noise to
mapd, thus causing channel planning follow the R1 logic.

7.2           Channel Planning feature details
7.2.1         Message flow
When a new device is detected in the network, controller will send it a Channel Preference Query. After receiving
a Channel Preference Report, controller will try to find the best possible channel as per our algorithm.
The best possible channel for a radio as per MAP R1 channel planning is:

 After selecting the best channel, controller will send the Channel Selection Request to the agent. Agent
 reconfigures the radio to the new channel and respond with Channel Operating report.

 If the channel preference list provided by the agent does not contain any channel which preferred other agents,
 then it will continue to operate on its existing channel.

 All logic to do channel planning is present at controller side. Agent if present in network, helps controller to
 gather channel condition information. Agent acts as a slave here and only responds to controller’s requests.
 Agent listens and responds to controller’s below requests:
               • Do scan and sent back scan report of particular channel list
               • Switch to channel to do CAC and send back CAC response
               • Ch selection request to switch to a particular channel

 Both agent and controller perform channel scan at each radio to gather all channels condition information. If no
 agent is present in network, then also controller is capable of doing channel planning by doing all of the above
 processes by itself.

Please Note:
 Channel configuration in MAP is taken care by Channel planning feature. Hence, boot up channel selected by
 AutoChannel in any case is not used. So AutoChannel feature should be kept disabled when MAP is enabled.

 7.2.2         When is channel planning run

                • Bootup Run for channel planning:
          After “ChPlanningInitTimeout”, controller will run channel planning once for each radio. At this time if
 there is any agent already connected to controller it will also help controller to do channel planning. So after

 planning logic. If any new devices joins the network after bootup run is complete then after its
 “ChPlanningInitTimeout”, its radio’s will also sync to this bootup time best channel.

                 • Current channel overload triggered channel planning:
           After bootup run network will stay at current best channel under normal circumstances.
 If due to some traffic the conditions of current best channels on any radio vary adversely, then controller can go
 for monitoring the current channel and later on to run channel planning if all conditions are met.

                • User trigger channel planning:
           Channel planning can be forcefully run via mapd_cli command. This will not do any channel monitoring,
 but start searching for a better channel than the current one by instantly running channel planning.

7.2.3         Channel planning stages
These are the stages as defined by Map R2 channel planning algorithm.

7.2.3.1       Channel Monitoring
Channel Monitoring is important because sometimes high utilization surges can occur, which may not last for
long durations, or they are like a false alarm. So it is important that the current channel be monitored for at least
“ChPlanningR2MonitorTimeoutSecs” duration. At the end of this duration, the averaged data collected during
the monitor interval will be analyzed and compared with the overload thresholds again. For threshold details
you can refer to the section 7.3.4. If now also it exceeds thresholds then it means channel planning need to run.

•  Channel monitoring prohibit interval:
         We also have a prohibit timer “ChPlanningR2MonitorProhibitSecs” which is configurable so that we
can have some gap between two monitoring runs. So we must stay on a particular channel for at least the prohibit
duration before we can decide to run monitoring/channel planning again.

•   Idle MAP network:
          Before channel monitoring starts, it is mandatory that “MAP network is in idle state” otherwise results
will not be consistent.

•   Limitation with channel monitoring
         When overlapping BSS is using only secondary channels for uplink and downlink traffic, then if this traffic
is overloading the secondary channel then also channel planning monitoring will not get triggered. This is
because it is a hardware limitation to detect high utilization on secondary channels. Eg: If a MAP network is on
channel 36 with 160MHz bandwidth (occupying channel 36 to 64) and OBSS traffic is running on channel 52 with
80MHz bandwidth, then channel utilization will not show high utilization on channel 36 due to this HW limitation.
Hence the channel monitoring cannot be triggered.

7.2.3.2       Channel Scanning
After the monitor duration is over controller decides whether to go to the next step for channel planning which
is to do channel scan. If channel planning is required then, controller gathers the information about all the
channels.
     • Each channel’s score and rank is calculated internally by the channel planning algorithm which makes
         use of the channel conditions found by the controller.
     • The higher the rank the better the channel. It is possible that two or more channels can have same
         rank/score. In this case any one of them can be chosen.
     • In 5G case it is also possible that you find that rank of a DFS channel is the highest. If the algo decides
         to move to that DFS channel, then user may have to wait for at least 65sec to see its effect on each
         device. This is because first DFS CAC will be done on this new channel and only if no radar was found on
         it , then the command to switch to this channel will be given by the controller to all devices and itself.
         Please refer to the DFS CAC R2 section for more details.

be described in two parts Initialization and requested scan :

7.2.4         Channel Planning with BW consideration
If this feature is enabled, then the channel planning best channel selection decision, will not just be based on
individual channel ranks, but also on the ranks of the complete bandwidth group to which this channel belongs
to.
Example if controller is currently operating on bandwidth 80MHz (channel 36), that means controller can occupy
all channels from 36 to 48. If 36 is found to be the worst channel and 48 is found to be the best channel by the
algo, still overall group rank of Band 36 to 48 can fall due to the score of channel 36.In this case if another band
say 149 to 161 is having better rank than the band 36 to 48 by a certain margin (ChPlanningR2MinScoreMargin)
then algo will choose band 149 to 161 for its operation.
This feature is used in 5G and 6G bands. Based on controller’s BW the groups are formed with available channels
as per preference of all devices. Then group score determins the best channel group as per the existing BW.
           Note: This feature should be kept off if the channel score display on web UI is used for demonstration.


7.2.5         User Preferred Channel Configuration
Mediatek Multi-AP turnkey solution provides a mechanism to configure the whole network on a user defined
channel. If a channel is marked as user preferred, best channel selection logic mentioned in 4.8.2 will not be
used. Instead use defined channel will carry the maximum weightage and controller will attempt to configure all
agents on user preferred channel.
If the user preferred channel is not present in an agent’s Channel Preference Report, channel to this particular
agent will not be assigned. In all other cases user preferred channel will always be the first preference. The
configuration interfaces are mentioned in below sections.

7.2.6         RADAR Handling in channel planning
MAP Turnkey feature uses channel planning feature to handle RADAR detection on any agent in the network. An
agent leverages dual backhaul system to convey RADAR detection to the controller.
Flow is as follows:
    1. Any agent which detects RADAR on 5G BH will form link on 6G BH or 2.4G BH or other 5G BH if tri-
         band according to priority.
    2. Agent will select a new random channel for 5G Hz from the valid channels in that band.
               a. The channel might be DFS or non-DFS channel.
    3. Agent will add this channel info in its CSA IE and move to this channel after CSA time.
               b. Connected clients should automatically move with it.
    4. Agent will send new channel preference report to controller using 6G or 2.4G BH informing presence
         of RADAR on a channel.
    5. Controller detects RADAR from channel preference report and triggers channel planning again to find
         an operable channel from channel preference report.
    6. Controller will send channel selection request to an agent using 6G BH or 2.4G BH or other 5G BH.
    7. Agent configures new channel. They will do a CSA first and set this new channel’s information in CSA IE

         default value in variable – NtwrkOptConnectWaitTime, NtwrkOptDisconnectWaitTime) on 2.4G or 5G
         (Tri-Band) connection.
    9. Network opt will switch the Agent BH channel to 5G once it finds out 5G channel is better.

7.2.8         Divergent channel planning
This MAP feature is used for forcefully switching a particular MAP device’s channel by the user after giving
channel and ALMAC for that device as input. The aim of this feature is to do a forceful channel switch, of any one

for individual radio of an agent. The command will not be processed for a radio on which an ApCli interface exist
in connected state. If the user triggers divergent channel planning API, convergent channel planning will be
disabled unless it is explicitly enabled using enable_ch_planning API.Details and usage of divergent channel
planning API are present in subsequent sections.

To use this feature in MAP R2, user will need an additional flag (flag name DivergentChPlanning ) to be set before
hand in mapd_user.cfg. By default this feature is disabled. The force channel switch mapd_cli command will be
acceptable by daemon in MAP R2 case only if this flag is set. Similar to the MAP version R1 implementation this
feature will mean that the convergent channel planning, based on channel conditions will not be able to run on
all MAP devices. This is because if this feature flag is enabled then it is assumed that the user wants to configure
each device’s channel separately via web UI or command

To use this feature in MAP ver. R1 when MAP R2 code is compiled ON, user will need an additional flag to be set
before hand in mapd_user.cfg. By default this feature is disabled, (flag name DivergentChPlanning).

When the mesh network is made up of Multi Link devices (MLDs) then this feature is not supported. This is
because when MLD link is present between two Mesh devices then their channels should match on all links for

7.3           User Configurable Skip Channel List
The User Configurable Skip Channel List is a supporting feature of Channel planning. The user Configurable Skip
Channel List configuration allows every MAP device to provide its own set of channel list to the controller which
should be skipped, while selecting channel in controller. This is achieved by giving low score to channels in skiplist.
This is a proprietary feature as only MTK devices support it.
This feature allows each MAP device to provide a set of channel skip list.
Each Device uses a Vendor message to send skip list to the controller, when any topology change happens.
Then controller will take the super set of each list and its own list, while deciding the score of each channel.

If a user preferred channel is given then channel skiplist will be avoided for that channel. Channel planning give
first preference to user defined channel.

For 5G channel skiplist, MAX channel BW of MAP network will take care by controller.
Example: if 40 is present in channel skiplist and max channel BW is 40MHz. Then 36,40 both will not be allowed
in channel selection.

At boot time of controller skiplist will be avoided, but later when channel planning runs it will take care of skip
channel list.

If all channels are mentioned in the skip channel list, then boot time channel will be selected as the best channel.

If radar is found then skiplist will be considered but if all remaining channels are in skiplist then channel selected
can be random. Later it when channel planning runs it will consider the channel skiplist again.

7.4           DFS CAC
MAP R2 specification offers a mechanism to let the controller send channel availability check (CAC) request on a
specific DFS channel to any agent and get the response. As specified in MAP R2 Specification there are various
methods by which a device can perform CAC.
These methods are:
    • Continuous CAC → Perform CAC on main radio
    • Continuous with dedicated radio → Perform CAC on dedicated radio.
    • MIMO dimension reduced(Not supported on MTK devices)
    • Time sliced CAC (Not supported on MTK devices)

7.4.1         Switching Channel to DFS
MAP R2 Turnkey uses Coordinated CAC while switching channel to a DFS channel. Unlike MAP R1, MAP R2 will
first decide the device which would perform CAC and with what method using the Agent CAC Capabilities and
max BW supported by device. The device to perform CAC is chosen in a manner so that the existing network is
disturbed in the least possible manner. During CAC a device will not be able to Tx on the CAC channel for at least
65 secs and 605 secs for weather channels. If it is an agent that has to perform CAC on its main radio (continuous
CAC), then this will impact its 5G BH connectivity.
Controller will decide which device to perform CAC in the below manner:
      • Find max BW supported devices in the network.
      • If Controller is MAP R2 and supports max BW in the networks, and DEDICATED radio is supported then
              o Controller will do CAC on dedicated radio.
      • If Controller is MAP R2 and NO - DEDICATED radio is supported, then
              o Farthest R2 Agent of MAX BW supported of network with DEDICATED radio will do CAC.
              o Else, Farthest R2 Agent of MAX BW supported of network with REDUCED MIMO radio will do
                   CAC.
              o Else, Farthest R2 Agent of MAX BW supported of network with CONTINUOUS radio will CAC.
              o Else, Controller R2 which supports MAX BW supported of network will directly switch to DFS
                   channel and do CAC.
      • If Controller is MAP R2 and NO- DEDICATED radio supported and all other agents are MAP R1 supported
          then
              o Controller will switch directly and do CAC on main radio.
      • If Controller is MAP R1 and DEDICATED radio supported then
              o Controller will do CAC on dedicated radio
      • If Controller is MAP R1 and NO - DEDICATED radio supported
              o Controller will switch directly to the DFS channel and do CAC on main radio.


If Controller decides other device (Agent) in network to perform CAC, then Controller will send CAC Request to
that Agent. After this Agent will perform CAC either on dedicated radio or main radio according to its capability.
On Successful CAC Completion, Agent will respond CAC Completion report to controller. Controller will then send
the Channel Selection request to the agents starting from the last node of the network and corresponding to all
the inner nodes, so that no disconnection occurs while switching channel.

7.4.3         RADAR Detection
Radar Handling will change in MAP R2 due to the introduction of Coordinated CAC feature and dedicated radio.

7.4.3.1       Agent Radar Detection
    •     Any agent which detects RADAR on 5G BH will form link on 2.4G BH. Also Agent will select a new random
          channel for 5G Hz from the valid channels in that band which can be DFS or non-DFS channel. Connected
          clients should automatically move with it.
    •     Agent will send new channel preference report to controller using 2.4G BH informing presence of RADAR
          on a channel.
    •     As Controller detects RADAR from channel preference report, it triggers MAP R2 channel planning again
          to find an operable channel from channel preference report.
    •     If that Channel is non-DFS then Controller will switch channel on agents through Channel selection
          request and bring back to 5GH after triggering Network Optimization.
    •     If that Channel is DFS then Controller will decide which device will do CAC and by what CAC method. If
          any agent is selected then it will send CAC Request to that agent. If controller supports Dedicated radio
          then it will do CAC (Refer 7.4.2)
    •     On Successful CAC Completion Agent will respond CAC Completion report to controller.
    •     Controller will then send the Channel Selection request to the agents starting from the last node of the
          network and corresponding to all the inner nodes, so that no disconnection occurs while switching
          channel.
    •     On CAC Completion Controller will also trigger network optimization to bring back the connection from
          2.4G to 5G

7.4.3.2       Controller Radar Detection
    •     If Controller detects Radar, then it will select a new random channel for 5G Hz from the valid channels
          in that band which can be DFS or non-DFS. If new channel is non-DFS then Controller will make BH on
          that new channel.
    •     If this new channel is DFS and Dedicated radio is supported on controller then, controller will do CAC on
          dedicated radio, making connection for further agents on default channel.
    •     If this new channel is DFS and Controller does not support Dedicated radio then, controller have to do
          CAC on main radio and will make BH on 2.4G.
    •     Controller triggers MAP R2 channel planning after 10 sec to find an operable channel from channel
          preference report.
    •     If that Channel is non-DFS then Controller will switch channel on agents through Channel selection
          request and bring back to 5GH after triggering Network Optimization.

there are two channel groups possible when BW is kept as 160. For example see picture of channel groups based
on BW as below (source: internet):

Even if one channel in the entire channel group is DFS, then CAC needs to be done for the entire group always.
So even if we want to switch to channel 36, still CAC will have to be done for the group 36 to 64( complete
160MHz) .

At bootup:
A device may bootup at a DFS or non-DFS channel as per setting inside the .dat file. But the BW setting in .dat
file is important to note. If the channel group formed by that BW includes even one DFS channel , then the device
will first do DFS CAC for that entire channel group. So you may experience some delay in connection allowed by
the 5G Band because of this reason.
For example:
               • If device bootups at channel 36 and 160MHz BW , and the first connection is made at 2.4G
                    Backhaul, this may be due to case that 5G radio of controller is doing CAC at that time ( even if
                    primary channel is non-DFS). After network optimization run when CAC completes BH may shift
                    on 5G BH based on network optimization decision. This is the expected behavior.

User preferred channel setting:
A user may set the primary channel of the device forcefully by mapd_cli commands or web UI. At this time the
user can choose any channel (DFS or non-DFS). Attempt will be made to make device attain maximum bandwidth
possible as per settings(channel preference). Hence upgrade or downgrade of Bandwidth is possible at this time.
So DFS CAC will be done if needed in this case.

8       Traffic Separation and Service Prioritization

8.1           Traffic Separation
8.1.1         Introduction
Traffic separation is mainly used to divide the whole MAP network into several sub networks by VLAN technique.
The sub networks with different VLAN id cannot communicate with each other. However all the sub networks
can access to the internet. There is one primary VLAN network and zero or more secondary VLAN networks.
Controller would announce the traffic separation policy to all the agents by auto-configuration or renew
procedure to partition VLAN networks. The policy contains a series of the SSID names and the corresponding
VLAN ids together with one primary VLAN id. Agents will assign the VLAN id to all the fronthaul BSSs based on
the relationship between SSID names and VLAN ids by policy. Ethernet LAN network belongs to primary network,
which means local Ethernet network can only communicate with WIFI primary network.

Here is a picture to help you understand more of the traffic separation feature.




                                        Figure 8- 1. Traffic Separation Image 1

Like the above network layout showing by picture, every MAP device starts up 4 WIFI interfaces and one of them
belongs to the primary network (SSID1), two of them belong to the secondary network (SSID2) and one of them
belong to the other secondary network (SSID3). The traffic flows are expected as below:
     a. NB and phone4 belongs to the primary network. They can communicate with each other but cannot
          communicate with phone1 ~phone3.
     b. Phone1 and phone2 belongs to the secondary network (vlan 20). They can communicate with each
          other but cannot communicate with phone3, phone4 and NB.
     c. Phone3 belongs to the other secondary network (vlan 30). It cannot communicate with phone1, phone2,
          phone4 and NB.
     d. All the STA devices, including phone1 ~phone4 and NB can access to internet.

8.1.2         Operating Mode
There are two types of operating mode, bridge mode and router mode. On bridge mode, WAN interface (eth1)
is bonded to bridge interface (br-lan). All the packets from WAN interface will be transferred directly to other

9       Stand-Alone Band Steering (Easy Mesh Disabled)

9.1           Introduction

Band Steering feature can work even if EasyMesh (MAP) is disabled.
This can be used in a:-
         1. Single AP deployment
         2. Legacy repeater network, where MAP is disabled on all the Access Points.

The algorithm works in exactly the same way as Agent Initiated Band Steering in a MAP network, with the
exception that the AP devices present in the network do not have to wait for a Steering Opportunity as in a MAP
network.
Every AP would perform Band Steering independently.



9.2           Components
Stand Alone Band Steering uses the same components as EasyMesh except that it doesn’t require the
1905Daemon and full-fledged MAP daemon(mapd). Following components are required: -
           • bs20: The Band Steering daemon, which is mapd minus the 1905 interface and with Multi-AP
               steering and MAP features disabled at run-time.
           • wapp
           • bs_cli
           • Driver

9.3           Feature details

There are three primary types of steering that are supported: -
        • Pre-association steering
        • Idle post-association steering
        • Active post-association steering.
                 o Active Non-Overloaded Steering
                 o Active Overloaded Steering

9.3.1         Pre-association steering
                   •
         •    Pre-association steering aims to connect dual band stations to a channel that is not overloaded. A
              channel is considered overloaded when its average medium exceeds pre-defined
              CUOverloadThreshold_XX (e.g. 70%) or the connected clients number exceed MaxClientOverloaded.
              While this condition holds, if the AP sees a dual band STA sending probe requests and the probe
              requests on the non-overloaded channel exceed a configurable threshold MinRSSIOverloaded (e.g.
              20 dB), a blacklist is installed and auth requests are rejected on the overloaded channel to
              encourage the STA to associate on the non-overloaded channel.
         •    If PHYBasedSelection option is set, the AP will also install blacklist statically on 5G channels to those
              dual band non-HT STAs.
         •    If that STAs try to connect to blacklisted BSS(es) more than AuthRejMax times, the existing pre-
              association should be aborted and allow the connection.

                                channel is non-overloaded. If the RSSI is quite old, the RSSI is refreshed by triggering a series of

                9.3.3            Active post-association steering.
                          •      An ACTIVE client is defined as a client for which the sum of Avg Tx Bytes/sec and Avg Rx Bytes/sec
                                 is greater than ActivityThreshold.
                          •      Only ACTIVE clients that are both 802.11K and 802.11V capable are eligible for steering
                          •      Only BTM steering is used for ACTIVE clients to cause minimum service disruption.
                          •      There are two types of steering that are defined for Active Clients:-
                                      o Active Non-Overloaded Steering
                                      o Active Overloaded Steering[Offloading]

                9.3.3.1          Active Non-Overloaded Steering
                          •      Active clients whose serving RSSI and DL MCS have increased above specific thresholds, are BTM
                                 steered to 5G band provided that the 5G channel is not overloaded and the steering of Active client
                                 doesn’t make the 5G channel as overloaded. 11k helps to predict the impact of moving the client
                                 to the target channel. If the Active client is known to fail BTM steering, then no steering is
                                 attempted.
                          •      Active clients whose serving RSSI and DL MCS have increased above specific thresholds, are BTM
                                 steered to 5G band provided that the 5G channel is not overloaded and the steering of Active client
                                 doesn’t make the 5G channel as overloaded. 11k helps to predict the impact of moving the client
                                 to the target channel. If the Active client is known to fail BTM steering, then no steering is
                                 attempted

                9.3.3.2          Active Overloaded Steering [Offloading]
                Active clients connected to an Overloaded channel are BTM steered to a non-overloaded channel provided that
                the steering of Active client doesn’t make the target channel as overloaded. 11k helps to predict the impact of
                moving the client to the target channel. If the Active client is known to fail BTM steering, then no steering is
                attempted

9.4           Limitations
             •    No Blacklisting coordination between the APs, if the RootAP and Repeaters share the same
                  SSID.
             •    As per design, Pre-association steering cannot happen till it it’s deduced that a client is Dual-
                  Band. Therefore, if the STA is using randomized address to scan, dual band capability of the
                  client can only be deduced after it connects to the AP.
             •    Pre-association Steering based on RSSI and channel load conditions (Non PHYbasedSelection
                  pre-steering) cannot happen, if the STA doesn’t send a Probe Request, before Sending 802.11
                  Authentication request. Probe request is required for the STA’s recent RSSI.
             •    Pre-association steering can sometimes fail with stations that use random mac address to
                  scan, and the time gap between their join probe-request and authentication request is too
                  short for our steering design to take a decision for blacklisting and rejecting authentication.
                  One such case has been observed with Huawei mate20 STA in which the Auth request is sent
                  within 4 ms of the Probe request. In such a scenario, some-times the STA is rejected
                  Association, and it never re-tries association.
             •    802.11r based fast transition not supported across bands. If FT is enabled on the DBDC AP, FT
                  capable station, when band steered, would fall back on non-FT Association.

11      Appendix

11.1          Configuration difference between LSDK and OpenWRT
MAP LSDK does not support persistent file system to store configurable parameters. Hence all configurations are
first stored onto the non-volatile memory space using the supported APIs. These configurations are then read
back using supported APIs from NVRAM and written into a file after reboot.

However OpenWRT SDK supports persistent file system. It is not required to write the configurations into the
NVRAM first. User can directly write into the configuration files to change the configuration and it will be retained
across reboot.

Majority of configuration examples present in this document are written keeping LSDK in mind. When extended
to OpenWRT SDK, the commands should be changed accordingly. The appropriate file where the configuration
parameter should be present against the configuration parameter.

An example of how a parameter is to be configured on two SDKs is below:

for LSDK
       ▪ nvram_set 2860 DeviceRole 2
for OpenWRT
       ▪ wificonf -f <config file path> set DeviceRole 2

    11.6          How to use WAPP daemon
    Start command:
    wapp -d1 -v2 –c<INF1_NAME> –c<INF2_NAME>

             INF1_NAME and INF2_NAME stands for two BSS interfaces on which 802.11R is supported.
             -c option is not required if 802.11R is not enabled on any interface.

    There are two processes created with different PID but same COMMAND name.
    WAPP supports multiple configuration files for different Wi-Fi interface (ex. ra0/ra1/ra2/rai0/rai1). Configuration
    files are used to initialize WAPP functions and default settings. It can be added in the file wapp_ap.conf. Currently,
    by default, only ra0 (wapp_ap_ra0.conf) is used to load all WAPP settings.

11.16         Sample Application for receiving events from MAP Daemon
A Sample application by the name “mapd_user_iface” is available which will continuously monitor user events
coming from MAP Daemon and print the Event type. The end user is free to update the action to be taken when
receiving the event, by modifying the sample application’s code.
To start this application use the below command:

./mapd_user_iface /tmp/mapd_ctrl

After giving this command the “mapd_user_iface” will continuously monitor all the supported user events. The
application parses the events in the below structure:
User event structure:

struct mapd_user_event
{
         int event_id;
         char event_body[0];
};

11.20         MAP integration with UCI system
The abbreviation UCI stands for Unified Configuration Interface and is a system to centralize the configuration of
OpenWrt services. Starting from the Eagle SKU , the Easymesh daemons will be using this UCI method to do all
configuration.

The main modifications done to support MAP configuration via UCI is as below :
    1. In new design we replace all easymesh file in UCI format so if any value written from WEB UI it should
        written in UCI file as shown below in /etc/config/ directory :
    2. Only the configurable parameters will get updated in these files.
    3. A new script /etc/uci2map.lua is created to convert the UCI files.

 4. Internally from the wapp daemon all the wireless related configuration to be set after onboarding will now
     be written in etc/config/wireless instead of .dat files as earlier implementation. This is because latest driver
